title: REPDF: Repairing corrupted PDF files through font mapping and object relationship reconstruction
venue: Forensic Science International: Digital Investigation 56, 302061 (DFRWS EU 2026)
summary: State of the art that PDFPundit is built on: byte-level object carving + template PDFs with a full-font database; dictionary-scored font inference; 1,000-file synthetic corpus (C1-C10); 90.67% mean text recovery.

title: REPDF dataset repository (dfrc-korea/REPDF): 100 original and 1,000 corrupted PDFs
summary: Corpus README (commit e547d4d, 2025-12-18). Clone to /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf (1.6 GB, git proxy). Suffix per class: _header _xref _trailer _page_tree _object_header _font_mapping_loss _remove_fonts _remove_unicode_fonts _stream_zlib _partial_cut.

title: qpdf source code (qpdf/qpdf)
summary: qpdf (Apache-2.0) at 4eba958. Rebuilds a broken xref by a full token scan (last copy of an object wins; trailer = newest with /Root, else largest XRef stream); does not carve ObjStm; recovers /Length by endstream/endobj search or empties the stream; writes undecodable streams unchanged; ignores Adler-32; missing /ID -> empty; US-Letter MediaBox default. Test corpus: 717 qtest PDFs + 78 OSS-Fuzz reproducers.

title: MuPDF source code (ArtifexSoftware/mupdf)
summary: MuPDF (AGPL-3.0-or-later, COPYLEFT: behaviour only) at d587982. Full-file repair on xref failure or object-number mismatch; carves ObjStm headers; later copies win except ObjStm vs later uncompressed copy; stops scanning at the first unparsable object once a root is known; keeps partial Flate output, ignores Adler-32, 200x bomb guard; font substitution by name/flags. No public test corpus.

title: pdf.js source code (mozilla/pdf.js)
summary: pdf.js (Apache-2.0) at d52fdf4. Recovery mode indexes all objects by scanning; picks the FIRST valid trailer with /ID; ObjStm only via surviving XRef streams; tolerant endstream search (misspelled/truncated forms); treats empty font files as missing; glyph-name ToUnicode heuristics; comments link each workaround to a regression PDF. Test corpus: 982 PDFs + 459 externally hosted .link PDFs.

title: PDFium source code (pdfium.googlesource.com/pdfium)
summary: PDFium (BSD-3-Clause) at 8ca5b73. RebuildCrossRef word scan incl. ObjStm members; highest generation wins, ties to later copy; /Length from nearer endstream/endobj, stream dropped if neither; Flate silently returns decoded prefix, 1 GiB cap; missing /ID -> empty; Arial-based substitute face. Test corpus: 341 PDFs + 562 .in templates.

title: Poppler source code (freedesktop poppler)
summary: Poppler (GPL-2.0-or-later, COPYLEFT: behaviour only) at c8dc23d. Line-start scan for trailer/endstream plus object headers, then XRef/ObjStm parsing; gen>= rule (ObjStm index used as gen); stream end from recorded endstream table after reconstruction; own inflater keeps partial output; base-14/system font substitution; numeric glyph-name heuristics; missing /ID -> empty. Test PDFs are in poppler/test (SRC-0506).

title: Ghostscript/GhostPDL source code (ArtifexSoftware/ghostpdl)
summary: Ghostscript/GhostPDL pdfi (AGPL-3.0-or-later, COPYLEFT: behaviour only) at a3cc9bd. One-shot repair that requires '%PDF' somewhere in the file; last copy wins, ObjStm members override, highest-numbered Catalog becomes Root; always verifies /Length and rescans; ignores Adler-32; enumerated error/warning taxonomy; missing /ID tolerated. No public regression corpus.

title: Poppler test-file repository (poppler/test)
summary: Poppler's test PDFs (83 files, mostly feature tests: signatures, forms, encryption) kept outside the main repo, commit 48b6219. Repository COPYING is GPL-2.0 for the harness code; per-file PDF licences unstated (NOASSERTION): analysis only, never redistribute.

venue: Journal of Cybersecurity Education, Research and Practice 2024

title: Improved recovery and reconstruction of DEFLATEd files
summary: Title-level: recovery and reconstruction of DEFLATE-compressed files; cited by Force Open (SRC-0127) as pattern-based repair of corrupted DEFLATE data that can partially reconstruct content using knowledge of the content (e.g. English text), and by SRC-0132 for mid-stream damage defeating reconstruction. Not read by this agent (sciencedirect 403); scoping-compression cached and read it as SRC-0301 from a dfrws.org copy, so at merge set this record duplicate_of SRC-0301. Earlier paper: Brown 2011 'Reconstructing corrupt DEFLATEd files' (10.1016/j.diin.2011.05.015, not screened). Direct prior art for GAP-005.

title: A forensic analysis of the Google Home: repairing compressed data without error correction
summary: Real forensic case: a Google Home NAND dump read without the SoC's undisclosed ECC. Corrupted gzip fragments are repaired by brute-forcing 1-2 bit flips with the zlib Adler-32 as oracle, lifting recovered data from 8.32% to 99.68%; ambiguous repairs are merged with three-valued logic (indeterminate bits). Read via arXiv 2210.00856 (author-modified version). Code: github.com/enssec/squashfs_bitflip_repair.

title: Force Open: Lightweight black box file repair
summary: Black-box file repair (DFRWS EU 2017): learns branches that behave identically for valid files and forces them when a viewer opens a corrupted file. Evaluated on PNG, JPG and PDF (viewer pdftotext, baseline pdftk) with synthetic random-byte overwrites; repaired sets overlap little with the baseline's. Read from the ETH Research Collection copy (CC BY-NC-ND).

title: Standardization of file recovery classification and authentication
summary: Title-level (not read, paywalled): a proposed standard classification for how recovered files were obtained, plus their authentication. From memory (unverified lead): distinguishes e.g. allocated, metadata-recovered and carved files. Closest forensic precedent to the charter's six provenance grades; 18 OpenCitations citing works, none on document repair (titles checked 2026-09-27).

title: Digital Investigation Techniques: A NIST Scientific Foundation Review

Free US-government publication. DOI 10.6028/NIST.IR.8354 is kept as an alias because Crossref truncates its title to 'Digital investigation techniques :', which fails the validator's DOI-title match. Discovery: known from memory, then confirmed in the citation network (it cites Lyle 2010, SRC-0131; OpenCitations, SRCH-0105).

OA (CC BY-NC).

title: Predict Responsibly: Improving Fairness and Accuracy by Learning to Defer
summary: Learning when an automated model should defer to a downstream human decision-maker.

title: On optimum recognition error and reject tradeoff
summary: Chow's optimal error-versus-reject trade-off: reject when the top posterior falls below a threshold.

title: Availability of datasets for digital forensics – And what is missing
summary: Survey of available digital-forensics datasets and what is missing; cites Brown 2011.

title: High-Throughput FPGA-Based Hardware Accelerators for Deflate Compression and Decompression Using High-Level Synthesis
summary: FPGA DEFLATE compression/decompression accelerators.

title: Forensic analysis techniques for fragmented flash memory pages in smartphones
summary: Forensic analysis of fragmented flash memory pages in smartphones.

title: Repair benchmark (DataRecover Pro): 30 synthetically corrupted JPEG, PNG, GIF, MP4, PDF and DOCX files
summary: Vendor-published 30-file repair benchmark.

title: An error-resilient blocksorting compression algorithm
summary: Error-resilient block-sorting (BWT) compression.

title: A Study on a Carving Method for Deleted NTFS Compressed Files
summary: Carving deleted NTFS (LZNT1) compressed files.

title: preflate-rs: lossless re-compression of DEFLATE streams (bit-exact re-creation from plaintext plus reconstruction parameters)
summary: Rust library that predicts a DEFLATE encoder's decisions and stores only the deviations, so the exact original bitstream can be recreated from the decoded data. Licence and commit not yet pinned.

title: Research Report: Building a Wide Reach Corpus for Secure Parser Development
summary: SafeDocs/JPL corpus-building report: ~30M PDFs gathered from Common Crawl (with re-pulls of truncated files), Sparkler crawls and issue-tracker APIs (Ghostscript Bugzilla, PDFBox/Tika JIRA). Documents Common Crawl's 1 MB truncation (22% of PDFs in the Dec 2019 crawl). Targeted extraction only.

title: Caradoc: A Pragmatic Approach to PDF Parsing and Validation
summary: Caradoc: crafted-file study of 6 readers (crashes, CPU exhaustion, cross-reader inconsistencies incl. duplicate keys, #-escapes, generation numbers), a restricted PDF grammar, a type checker, and a relaxed-parser normalizer. On 10,000 web PDFs only 1,465 pass the strict parser; most use incremental updates; normalization rewrote 8,993 files but drops objects unreachable from the trailer.

title: Shadow Attacks: Hiding and Replacing Content in Signed PDFs
venue: Proceedings 2021 Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
summary: Shadow attacks on signed PDFs: standard-compliant incremental updates that Hide, Replace or Hide-and-Replace content after signing (incl. two objects with the same object number switched via a later xref). 16 of 29 viewers vulnerable. PDF-Detector compares the signed revision with the final one; evaluated only on 26 self-generated files.

title: On the correctness of electronic documents: studying, finding, and localizing inconsistency bugs in PDF readers and files
summary: Cross-reader inconsistency study on Govdocs1: manual first-page comparison of 2,313 random files in 8 readers finds 13.5% rendered inconsistently; automated error-clustering + CW-SSIM + delta-debugging pipeline over 230K files finds 30 unique bugs. Future work: automatically fixing PDF files, which they note is hard because of xref offsets and object numbering. Cached copy is the authors' self-archived PDF (srg.doc.ic.ac.uk); Springer serves a JS challenge to urllib.

title: Looking for non-compliant documents using error messages from multiple parsers
summary: Uses co-occurrence of error messages from ~20 PDF parser configurations (caradoc, hammer, pdfium, xpdf, pdfminer, qpdf, veraPDF, ...) to flag non-compliant files. Ground truth: expert-marked SafeDocs T&E corpus; 1,794 of 9,000 Common Crawl files marked 'rejected' (non-compliant or malicious). Argues benign-but-non-compliant files are dangerous because parsers repair them differently.

title: CC-MAIN-2021-31-PDF-UNTRUNCATED corpus README (SafeDocs, tballison/CC-MAIN-2021-31-PDF-UNTRUNCATED)
summary: README of the SafeDocs CC-MAIN-2021-31-PDF-UNTRUNCATED corpus (~7.9M unique PDFs, digitalcorpora.org), pinned at commit b21a137. Provenance table gives Common Crawl's truncation flag per URL (length: 2,020,913; disconnect: 5,861), refetch status (REFETCHED_SUCCESS: 1,922,505) and the WARC file/offsets of the original (truncated) capture - i.e. candidate natural pairs of truncated capture + later full fetch.

title: Demystifying PDF through a machine-readable definition
venue: LangSec Workshop at IEEE S&P 2021 (work in progress)
summary: Arlington PDF Model: machine-readable (TSV) definition of PDF 2.0 objects and key relationships (langsec.org abstract: 514 objects, 3,551 keys/array elements), validated against a corpus of extant files and used to find extant-data malformations. Candidate structural oracle for 'conforming' output and for type-guided repair.

title: Research Report: Strengthening Weak Links in the PDF Trust Chain
summary: Galois + PDF Association: formal definition of how PDF cross-reference data is constructed, with multiple complex dialects; producing it raised spec issues acknowledged by the PDF Association (langsec.org abstract).

title: Daedalus: Safer Document Parsing
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages
summary: Daedalus DSL/toolchain for safe parsers with stream-manipulation constructs for non-contiguous formats (Crossref abstract); (memory, unverified) includes a PDF parser developed under SafeDocs.

title: The Pitfalls of Protocol Design: Attempting to Write a Formally Verified PDF Parser
summary: Attempted Coq-verified PDF parser; per Caradoc (SRC-0202) it exposed spec ambiguities such as mutually-referencing incremental updates (cyclic /Prev chains).

title: 1 Trillion Dollar Refund
venue: Proceedings of the 2019 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security
summary: '1 Trillion Dollar Refund: How To Spoof PDF Signatures' (CCS 2019): per SRC-0203 it introduced Incremental Saving Attacks that append malformed incremental updates; (memory, unverified) also signature wrapping and universal signature forgery.

title: Breaking the Specification: PDF Certification
venue: 2021 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
summary: Attacks on certified PDFs (S&P 2021); (memory, unverified) Evil Annotation and Sneaky Signature attacks via permitted incremental updates.

title: Processing Dangerous Paths – On Security and Privacy of the Portable Document Format
venue: Proceedings 2021 Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
summary: Processing Dangerous Paths (NDSS 2021); (memory, unverified) denial-of-service, information disclosure, data manipulation and code execution via standard PDF features across many processors.

title: Extract Me If You Can: Abusing PDF Parsers in Malware Detectors
venue: Proceedings 2016 Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
summary: Extract Me If You Can (NDSS 2016); (memory, unverified) parser-confusion attacks exploiting differences between malware detectors' PDF parsers and Adobe Reader.

title: Content Disarm and Reconstruction of PDF Files
summary: Content Disarm and Reconstruction of PDF Files (IEEE Access 2023, CC BY-NC-ND).

title: Toward the Detection of Polyglot Files
venue: Proceedings of the 15th Workshop on Cyber Security Experimentation and Test
summary: Toward the Detection of Polyglot Files (CSET 2022); (memory, unverified) evaluates file-type identification tools against polyglots including PDF.

title: On the Abuse and Detection of Polyglot Files
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Web Conference 2025
summary: On the Abuse and Detection of Polyglot Files (WWW 2025).

title: PolyDoc: Surveying PDF Files from the PolySwarm network
summary: PolyDoc: PDFs gathered from the PolySwarm network traced through mutool, Poppler and Caradoc and labelled with the PDF Error Ontology; reports syntactic malformations in files classified as malicious (langsec.org abstract).

title: A Format-Aware Reducer for Scriptable Rewriting of PDF Files
summary: Format-aware reducer and scriptable Parsley normalizations for PDF files, noting other popular PDF transformation tools do not apply them (langsec.org abstract).

title: Research Report: The Parsley Data Format Definition Language
summary: Parsley data format definition language (SafeDocs); the basis of the Parsley PDF checker (per SRC-0219's abstract).

title: A Survey of Parser Differential Anti-Patterns
summary: A Survey of Parser Differential Anti-Patterns (SPW 2023).

title: Corpus-wide Analysis of Parser Behaviors via a Format Analysis Workbench
summary: Corpus-wide Analysis of Parser Behaviors via a Format Analysis Workbench (SPW 2023); cites SRC-0201 and SRC-0205.

title: Research Report: Building a File Observatory for Secure Parser Development
summary: SafeDocs File Observatory (2021); (memory, unverified) runs many parsers over the SafeDocs corpora and indexes their outputs/exceptions.

title: Research Report: Progress on Building a File Observatory for Secure Parser Development
summary: Progress report on the SafeDocs File Observatory (2022); per the langsec.org abstract it adds a bug-tracker corpus and new analytic methods.

title: Research Report: ICARUS: Understanding De Facto Formats by Way of Feathers and Wax
summary: ICARUS: understanding de facto formats (SPW 2020); cites Caradoc (OpenCitations).

summary: Seven Turrets of Babel: taxonomy of LangSec input-handling errors (SecDev 2016); cited by the seed.

summary: Hidden data in PDFs and the sanitization practice of security agencies (IH&MMSec 2021); cited by the seed.

summary: How far JHOVE's validity/well-formedness verdicts can be trusted (digital preservation, IJDC, CC BY).

title: Automatic input rectification
summary: Automatic input rectification (ICSE 2012): cited by SRC-0204 as prior repair work that uses image similarity to assess repaired input; (memory, unverified) learns constraints from typical inputs and rewrites atypical inputs to satisfy them.

title: Exposing Vulnerabilities in PDF Malware Detectors to Evasion Attacks
summary: Evasion of ML PDF malware detectors.

title: pdf-association/pdf-corpora README: an index of PDF-centric corpora
summary: README of the PDF Association's index of PDF-centric corpora (github.com/pdf-association/pdf-corpora, pinned at commit d7feb03). Documents the SafeDocs Issue Tracker ('stressful') corpus (>32K PDFs from bug-tracker attachments, rich in malformed files; downloadable from corpora.tika.apache.org) and UNSAFE-DOCS (>5.0M files incl. a Common Crawl component with truncated PDFs and files generated by Kudu Dynamics' Voice of the Offense team), plus GovDocs1, IUST-PDFCorpus and others.
